paper_title: How to Generate Popular Post Headlines on Social Media
caption: The average similarities between the headlines from different seasons
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the average similarity (scaled by 10⁻²) between social media post headlines across five consecutive time intervals, labeled on the x-axis as Δ Days: (0,90], (90,180], (180,270], (270,360], and (360,450]. The y-axis, labeled “Avg. similarity (10e-2)”, ranges from 1.70 to 1.85 with tick marks at 0.05 intervals. A single light blue dashed line with circular markers connects five data points, each representing the average similarity for a given time interval. The similarity begins at approximately 1.84 for the first interval (0,90], decreases to 1.80 at (90,180], drops further to 1.72 at (180,270], rises slightly to 1.74 at (270,360], and then declines to 1.68 at (360,450]. A light blue shaded region surrounds the line, indicating a confidence interval or error band that widens slightly at the endpoints and narrows around the middle intervals.
